overview: Interior designers plan the look, function and safety of indoor spaces such as homes, offices, hospitals and stores. They meet clients, sketch ideas, choose colors, furniture and materials, produce drawings in CAD software and check building and accessibility codes. O*NET rates knowledge of design at 4.88 out of 5 for this job and building and construction at 4.24. Most hold a bachelor's degree, 84% in O*NET data, and some states require a license. The BLS May 2025 median is $67,190 across 71,500 jobs. Deadlines are tight and many designers are self-employed.
pay: Interior designers earn a median of $67,190, and the top 10% earn $114,140 or more. The District of Columbia has the highest state median at $98,450, 47% above the national figure, followed by Wyoming at $96,100. California has the most jobs, 8,500, at a median of $80,230.

faq.q: How much do interior designers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $67,190 a year. The middle half earn between $51,840 and $85,740. The District of Columbia, Wyoming and California pay the most, while West Virginia ($49,800) and Mississippi ($43,740) have the lowest state medians. Commercial design often pays more than residential.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be an interior designer?
faq.a: Most interior designers hold a bachelor's degree, 84% in O*NET data, in interior design or interior architecture. There are 7 related majors. Some states require a license, which usually means passing the NCIDQ exam after a few years of work experience.

faq.q: What skills do interior designers need?
faq.a: O*NET rates speaking, critical thinking, reading comprehension and active listening at 4 out of 5 for this job. Knowledge of customer service is rated 4.48, since you turn client wishes into plans. Innovation stands out as a work style, along with CAD skills.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to interior designer?
faq.a: Landscape Architects are an 83% match and earn $79,870, 19% more. Architects are a 72% match and earn $99,280, 48% more, according to BLS May 2025 data, but need an architecture degree and license. Architectural drafters are a 77% match.
